facts.text: Mebane takes its name from Brigadier General Alexander Mebane, a North Carolina militia officer who served in Congress during the 1790s.
The arrival of the railroad in 1855 sparked Mebane’s growth, leading to its 1881 incorporation as Mebanesville.
The Mebane Historical Museum curates the town’s cultural heritage through exhibitions, events, and educational programs that celebrate local history.
Several Mebane landmarks, including the Mebane Commercial Historic District and the Old South Mebane Historic District, are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Mebane ranks among North Carolina’s fastest-growing municipalities, reflecting rapid development over recent decades.
Mebane’s location straddles two TV markets, so residents receive stations from both the Triad and Triangle regions.
